summary: W. Norman Brown was an Indologist and historian who studied at Hiram College and Johns Hopkins University under Maurice Bloomfield and Franklin Edgerton. He held posts at Johns Hopkins, Government Gandhi Memorial Science College, and the University of Pennsylvania (1926–1966).
W. Pachow is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Indology who studied under Tan Yun-shan. He held a teaching and research post at Visva-Bharati University.

W. Randolph Kloetzli is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago in 1964. He has lectured at American University, George Washington University, and Dartmouth College.

W. S. Karunatillake was a scholar of linguistics and Buddhist studies. He was a professor at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1997) and served as Visiting Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard Divinity School in 1998.

Wai Lun Tam is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology who completed his PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara. By 2016, he was a professor and department chairperson at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Walpola Rahula (1907–1997) was a Buddhist studies and history scholar who studied at Calcutta, Ceylon, and Paris under Paul Demiéville. He held posts at Northwestern University (1964), University of Sri Jayewardenepura (1964–1969), and University of Oxford (~1974–1977).

Walter Bruno Henning (1908–1967) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Göttingen. He held posts at SOAS/University of London (~1936–1961), Columbia University (~1946–1947), and UC Berkeley (~1961–1967).

Walter Elliot (1803–1887) was a scholar in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics who studied at East India Company College and the College of Fort St George. He served as Private Secretary to Lord Elphinstone in Madras (1837–1842).

Walter Eugene Clark (1881–1960) was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Harvard and under Richard Pischel. He held posts at the University of Chicago (1915–1927) and Harvard University (1927–1950).

Walter Liebenthal (1886–1982) was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who received his doctorate from Breslau. He held posts at Peking University (1937), Visva-Bharati University (1952, 1959), Hebrew University (1959), and University of Tübingen (1965–1982).

Walter M. Spink (1928–2019) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Amherst College and Harvard University. He taught at Brandeis University (1956–1961) and served as professor at the University of Michigan (~1961–2000).

Walter Nowick (1926–2013) was a Buddhist studies figure who attended the Juilliard School and studied under Zuigan Goto from 1950 to 1965. He taught at Kyoto Women's University and founded Moonspring Hermitage.

Walter Porzig (1895–1961) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Jena under Wilhelm Streitberg. He held academic posts at Leipzig (~1923–1925), Bern (~1925–1935), Jena (~1935–1945), and Mainz (~1951–1961).

Walter Ruben (1899–1982) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He held academic posts at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1931–1935), the University of Chile (~1948–1950), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1950–1965).

Walter Simon (1893–1981) was a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at Humboldt University (1919–1937) and SOAS/University of London (1936–1960), where he became Professor of Chinese.

Walter Slaje is an Indologist who completed his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Vienna. He worked at Graz University Library (1984–1995) and served as director at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from 1995 to 2020.

Walter William Skeat (1835–1912) was a linguistics scholar who studied at Christ's College, University of Cambridge (~1854–1858). He later held a post at the University of Cambridge from approximately 1878 until 1912.

Walter Yeeling Evans-Wentz (1878–1965) was a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Stanford University (~1902–1907) and the University of Oxford (1907), later studying as a disciple under Kazi Dawa Samdup (~1919–1922).

Walther Heissig (1913–2005) was a Central Asian and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Vienna, Göttingen, and Bonn. He held positions at Peking University, Fu Jen Catholic University (~1941–1945), and the University of Bonn (from 1964).

Walther Schubring (1881–1969) was an Indologist who studied under Ernst Leumann at the University of Strasbourg. After working at the Prussian State Library in 1907, he held the Indology chair at the University of Hamburg from 1920 to 1951.
